# Draft:Moony Warfield

----
Moony Warfield is an American long-distance runner from Fort Collins, Colorado, known for competitive finishes in various races and aiming for the World Championships. They are an XTERRA series racer who identifies as a non-binary athlete and competes in both gender-neutral and non-binary divisions.
Assigned male at birth, they came out as transgender and nonbinary during pride month of June, 2021.
Career
High School
While attending Pacifica Christian High School Santa Monica, Warfield ran an 800 m in 2:18.71 (2020), a 1600 in 4:56.42 (2020), a 3200 in 10:31.33 (2020), a 5,000 track in 17:41.41 (2021), a 3 mile cross country in 16:29.50 (2019) and a 5,000 cross country in 17:05.00 (2019).
On the track Warfield would win the Liberty League Finals in the 1600 in 2021 and qualify to CIF-SS prelims for the 1600 in 2021. Warfield would as well as qualify for the 3200 at CIF-SS prelims in 2023 with a second place finish at the Liberty League Finals.
In cross country Warfield would qualify as apart of a team to CIF-SS Prelims and CIF-SS Finals in 2019, and 2021, Warfield would also individually qualify for CIF-SS Prelims in 2022 but not advance to the finals. Along with making CIF-SS finals in 2019 as a team Pacifica Christian High School would advance to the CIF State meet as well.
Outside Of High School
High School Years (2019-2023)
2020
In 2020, Warfield would race their first ever 10k at the L.A. Chinatown Firecracker 5k/10k. Warfield would place 9th in 36:52 out of over 2,600 participants. Warfield, who was 14 at the time, would win their age group of 11-14.
2022
In 2022, Warfield would race their first half marathon at the Surf City Half Marathon in 1:27:32. Placing 95th overall out of over 6,100 participants. They would stay steady for most of the race being at 94th through 5 miles, and 92nd through 9 miles. Warfield would also place 10th in their age group of 15-19 at 16 years old. Later that year Warfield would race the in person Nikki Hiltz Pride 5k in 21:00 placing 30th overall. They would win the nonbinary division in this race.
2023
In Spring 2023, Warfield would race the Victory for Victims 10k in 38:42.8 placing 2nd overall. There was no nonbinary division for this race so Warfield competed with the men.
Current Years (2023-Present)
2023
In 2023, Warfield would move to Fort Collins, Colorado and compete in a few more races. They would compete in the CSU Homecoming 5k placing 27th out of over 1,2000 participants in 17:35. They would also win the nonbinary division for the race. A few weeks later Warfield would race the Bell Ringer 4 miler in 23:35 to take second overall. There was no nonbinary division for this race so Warfield competed with the men.
2024
In 2024, Warfield would join the Fort Collins Run Club race team and would begin their season in March with the Lucky Brew Race 15k with their new team and get second overall in 57:52.01. They would win the nonbinary division in this race. Their next race would be the Horsetooth Half Marathon. Warfield would again run under the Fort Collins Run Club race team and place 72nd out of over 2,000 participants with a time of 1:33:48.22. Warfield would win the nonbinary division for this race.
In May, Warfield would race the 43rd Annual Providence Saint John's Health Center Brentwood Run 10k. Warfield would place 5th overall in 37:30 and win their age division as well. There was no nonbinary division so Warfield competed with the men. Warfield would run under Fort Collins Run Club race team in August as apart of the Lory Summer Trail Series competing in two of the four races. This was the first trail race for Warfield as they would run the Eltuck Valley 5k in 21:47.8 to place 15th overall. The following week would run the
Warfield would then come back to race the CSU Homecoming 5k with the Fort Collins Run Club race team placing 37th overall in 18:01.531 and winning the nonbinary category. Warfield would return to the Bell Ringer 4 miler again attached to the Fort Collins Run Club race team and win overall in 23:32. There was no nonbinary division in this race so Warfield competed with the men.
2025
In 2025, Warfield would open the season with the Horsetooth Half Marathon representing the Fort Collins Run Club race team placing 29th out of almost 2,000 participants in 1:22:41.55. Warfield would also win the nonbinary division for this race. Warfield would next race the Quad Rock 25 mile trail placing 48th overall in 5:07:18 and winning the nonbinary division. Warfield would then compete at the Xterra Deadwood Mickelson Trail Half Marathon placing 7th out of over 1,200 participants in 1:17:51. They would place second in their age group and there was no nonbinary division.
Warfield would move the track for a minute with a 3k steeplechase as well as the Men's Fort Collins Elite Mile for Fort Collins Run Club race team placing 5th before competing at the FireKracker 5k. Warfield would compete in the Elite field with Fort Collins Run Club race team but also as a nonbinary runner. They would place 36th overall in 16:46 and win the nonbinary division. Warfield would compete for the first time internationally at the Xterra Trail World Championships in Wales. Warfield would compete in the Half Marathon division placing 14th in 2:22:23 and would be the second American. Warfield would continue their season with the Choice City Running Festival - Human Race 10k placing 2nd overall in 37:31 and winning the nonbinary division.
Warfield would race the Black Squirrel Trail Half Marathon placing 20th overall in 1:57:19 and winning the nonbinary division. Warfield would return to the CSU Homecoming for the 3rd year straight placing 21st overall and winning the nonbinary division in 17:54.38. The next day Warfield would race the Blue Sky Trail Half Marathon placing 9th overall and winning the nonbinary division in 1:46:13. Warfield would race the Bell Ringer 2 Miler, a course change from the 4 miler, for the 3rd year in a row and win overall. There was no nonbinary category for this race.
